title: Effects of range of motion on resistance training adaptations: A systematic review and meta-analysis
publication: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
population: 16 studies of full versus partial range-of-motion training.
key_findings: Full range of motion gave larger strength gains (effect size 0.56) and larger lower-limb hypertrophy (effect size 0.88) than partial range.
Functional performance leaned towards full range without reaching significance.
Muscle architecture (thickness, pennation angle, fascicle length) did not differ significantly.
methods: Prospectively registered systematic review (PROSPERO) and meta-analysis with robust variance estimation; risk of bias with RoB 2 and certainty with GRADE.
limitations: Sixteen studies; the abstract compares full against partial range without separating where in the range partial repetitions were done.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
